reason: Two identical PROV-N statements, a hadMember with an identifier or an anonymous used with or without an attribute, come back from `unified()` as one record. `unified()` keeps each record once, so an instance is a set of statements (#548, #124).

Where an absent plan, derivation activity, or generation or usage of a derivation with no activity meets a present value, `unified()` raises ProvUnificationError with an exact message naming the first such position. PROV-CONSTRAINTS Definition 4 and Table 3 make these positions non-expandable (#547).
An agent and an entity with one identifier both stay after `unified()`, as two records. PROV-CONSTRAINTS Constraint 54 does not pair an agent with an entity, in the scope of #253.

Two associations with one identifier that differ in agent and in an absent plan raise ProvUnificationError that mentions conflicting values. #547 keeps the conflicting-values error ahead of the non-expandable check.

Two activities with one identifier and different startTimes make `unified()` raise `ProvUnificationError` whose message names the qualified identifier `ex:a` and startTime (PROV-CONSTRAINTS Constraint 22, #253). `test_unification_constraints.py::test_conflicting_start_times_fail_to_unify` was proposed as a takeover and does not cover it, because it uses a default-namespace identifier and asserts only its local part. The verifier planted two faults in the message built by `_unify_same_type_group`, one that writes the local part and one that writes the IRI of the identifier, and each failed only this test. The upgrade guide `docs/howto/prepare-for-3-3.md` (Read the message) says a `unified()` message starts with, or names, the identifier, with prefixed examples such as `ex:assoc`, and a message without the prefix cannot tell `ex:a` from `other:a`.

Two generations with one identifier and different entities make `unified()` raise `ProvUnificationError` (PROV-CONSTRAINTS Constraint 23, #253). The `generation-fail2` row of `test_unification_constraints.py::test_unified_corpus_characterization` takes over, because it raises from the same statement in `_unify_same_type_group`, reached through `_unified_records` and `_unify_record_group`, for the same cause, and also matches the message `has conflicting values`. `test_model.py::test_unifying` raises on the same shape from `unification-generation-f1-FAIL-c23.json`. The verifier planted a fault that skips the conflict check for a value that is a `QualifiedName`, and 20 tests failed it, among them that row. The row skips without lxml, which every CI job that runs it installs, and `test_model.py::test_unifying` still guards the shape then.

A derivation and an influence with one identifier stay as two records after `unified()`. PROV-CONSTRAINTS section 6.4 worked example, which exempts wasInfluencedBy from the disjointness of Constraint 53, in the scope of #253.
A generation and a usage with one identifier raise ProvUnificationError whose message names prov:Generation and prov:Usage. PROV-CONSTRAINTS Constraint 53, in the scope of #253.

An entity and an activity with one identifier raise ProvUnificationError whose message names prov:Entity and prov:Activity, in both orders of declaration. PROV-CONSTRAINTS Constraint 55 (entity-activity-disjoint), in the scope of #253.

Same-identifier statements with an absent expandable formal, equal plans or equal copies unify into one record. PROV-CONSTRAINTS Definition 4 keeps an absent value elsewhere an existential, and the rejecting rule of #547 sits beside this test.

Two associations with one identifier and different prov:time extra attributes raise ProvException that mentions more than one value, with an absent plan on one. #547 puts the non-expandable check after a successful merge.
A PROV-JSON hadMember with an identifier and two members gives two memberships after `unified()`. The PROV-JSON membership array with an identifier of #530 stays two relations under `unified()`.

A mention built with `new_record` under the identifier of an entity does not raise, and both records stay. PROV-DM gives a mention no identifier, so Constraint 54, which covers the eleven identified relations, does not apply (#253).

For each of hadMember, alternateOf, specializationOf and mentionOf, two PROV-N statements that share an identifier come back unchanged from `unified()`. PROV-DM gives these four relations no identifier, so there is nothing to merge on (#530).
An entity and a generation with one identifier raise ProvUnificationError whose message names prov:Entity and prov:Generation. PROV-CONSTRAINTS Constraint 54, in the scope of #253.

Two entities with one identifier merge into one entity with both attribute values, and a hadMember statement of that identifier stays. Records that do have an identifier keep merging beside a relation that has none (#530).

Two used statements that differ in one attribute value, in an absent formal against a time, or in an identifier stay two records after `unified()`. `unified()` drops only a record equal to an earlier one (#548, #124).

Two activities with one identifier, one with a startTime and one with an endTime, merge into one activity that holds both times and both extra attributes (PROV-CONSTRAINTS section 6.1, Constraint 22, #253). `test_unification_constraints.py::test_compatible_partial_information_merges_like_the_spec_example` takes over, because it builds the same example and asserts one record and its exact PROV-N text, which carries both times and both extra attributes that `_unify_same_type_group` merges for `_unified_records`. The datetime object against string input difference ends in `_ensure_datetime`, which `ProvBundle.activity` applies before the record exists. The verifier planted three merge faults in bundle.py (extra attributes from the first record only, formal values from the first record only, groups with a prefixed identifier skipped), and each failed the takeover or the vendored corpus rows. #253 does not list the worked example as its own shape. The takeover skips without lxml, which every CI job that runs it installs.

After `unified()` the first of two equal anonymous statements keeps its place among the records, and a later statement with an identifier follows. `unified()` keeps each record once and keeps the first of equal records (#548, #124).

An activity at the top level and an activity in a bundle with one identifier and different startTimes do not make `unified()` raise, and the result still has a bundle. PROV-CONSTRAINTS section 7.2 scopes unification to each bundle, and docs/explanation/unification-flattening.md says nothing merges across a bundle boundary.
